subject: social_science
chapter_title: State and Society up to 1000 CE

concepts.title: How State and Society Organised Themselves
concepts.definition: Before 1000 CE Indian society organised itself through kingdoms, varna-based social order and village communities: rulers collected taxes and protected land, Brahmanas, chiefs and guilds held influence, and local assemblies managed everyday affairs in many regions.
concepts.key_idea: King, community and custom together ran early states - power was shared, not absolute.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest105.txt opening sections (how society and state organised before 1000 CE)
question_patterns: how did society and state organise themselves prior to 1000 CE
what were the sources of revenue of early kingdoms
describe the role of village assemblies in early states
how was society divided in this period - describe the social order
what duties did a king perform according to the texts
compare the power of the king and the local assemblies

solution_steps.explain: Kings with court, army and revenue system governed territories.
Varna order, guilds and village communities structured daily life.
Assemblies and local chiefs limited and shared royal power.

concepts.title: Land, Revenue and Grants
concepts.definition: Land was the backbone of the early economy: peasants produced grain, a share went to the ruler as tax, and kings made land grants to Brahmanas and temples recorded on copper plates - grants that also pushed agriculture into new areas.
concepts.key_idea: Land fed the state; land grants bound kings, priests and temples in one economy.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest105.txt sections on land revenue and grants
question_patterns: what were land grants and why were they given
what do copper plate inscriptions record - explain
how did peasants support the early state system
what was the share of produce taken as tax
how did grants help spread agriculture
discuss the effects of land grants on society and polity

solution_steps.explain: Grain moved from peasant to state and temple as tax and offering.
Copper plates recorded grants, boundaries and privileges.
Grants created landed elites and expanded cultivation.

concepts.title: Trade, Cities and Cultural Life
concepts.definition: Guilds of merchants and craftspeople, busy port and inland cities, coinage and temple towns marked the economic vigour of the age, while Sanskrit, Prakrit and Tamil literatures, temples and philosophy enriched its cultural life up to 1000 CE.
concepts.key_idea: Trade fed cities, cities fed culture: economy and ideas grew together.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest105.txt sections on trade, cities and cultural life
question_patterns: what were guilds and what role did they play
describe the trade connections of early India
how did temple towns grow into economic centres
name the languages and literatures flourishing before 1000 CE
what was the role of ports in this period
describe the cultural achievements of the age with examples

solution_steps.explain: Routes linked coasts, cities and distant lands; coins eased exchange.
Merchant and craft guilds organised production and trade.
Temples, texts and tournaments of ideas filled the cities.
